narrative.overview:
The page is one pane of night window glass, seen from inside the shop after the lights are off. Deep blue-green glass fills every region inside a thin dark shopfront frame, lit from the top right by one lamp left on in the back. Headlines are white vinyl lettering applied straight to the glass. Everything a visitor reads closely or acts on is paper posted on that glass with a strip of gold tape: a grade placard, a request slip, a printed answer slip, a repair work order with a tear-off price stub, a price list with leader dots, a receipt.

Density is split by material. The glass carries one headline, one or two leads and a lot of dark space per section; the paper carries the detail at reading size, in navy ink. One typeface does all the work: Archivo, a variable grotesque, stretched wide for printed bands and labels and squeezed condensed for scores and prices, so the hierarchy comes from the width axis more than from a second family.

The confirmed rejection is the split SaaS hero with a dashboard screenshot and a row of feature cards. Nothing here is a generic card. Each sheet is a specific printed object with one job, and the score is posted the way an inspection grade card is posted in a shop window, readable from the street.
keyCharacteristics: One glass surface owns every region; light appears only as paper posted on it.
Two inks: white vinyl on glass, navy on paper.
Archivo variable across widths 62–125: condensed numerals, wide printed labels.
Square-cut paper (2px corners) lifted by one soft shadow and held by gold tape.
Pill buttons in three dresses: navy on paper, gold in the masthead, vinyl on open glass.
Motion plays once on arrival: a glare crosses the glass and the placard presses on; both are off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Glass Owns Every Region Rule
rules.body: No section switches to a light background. Every region sits on the glass gradient; light surfaces exist only as paper sheets posted on it.

rules.name: The Two Inks Rule
rules.body: On glass, text is White Vinyl or Frosted Vinyl. On paper, text is Placard Navy or Carbon Gray. Navy never letters the glass, and vinyl never prints on paper.

rules.name: The Tape Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold is tape and one glass-side signal (the masthead pill, the focus ring, selection). It never fills a sheet, never colors text, and never appears inside paper; inside paper the focus ring turns navy.

rules.name: The Width Is the Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Archivo's width axis carries role: 62% for numbers that score, rank or price; 104–108% for headlines and titles; 100% for reading text; 125% for the wordmark, printed labels, bands and the decal. Every number that scores or prices is condensed 800 with tabular figures.

rules.name: The Wide Caps Rule
rules.body: Uppercase appears only at 112–125% width with 0.04–0.1em tracking, and only on printed labels: a sheet's heading, the placard band, the verdict word, the stub caption, the footer decal. Headlines and reading text are never set in capitals.

rules.name: The One Sheet per Section Rule
rules.body: A section holds one headline and its lead on the glass and at most one paper sheet. The glass between sections stays empty except for the hairline that divides them.

rules.name: The Paper Lifts, Glass Stays Flat Rule
rules.body: Only paper casts a shadow, and every sheet casts the same one. Lettering on the glass never gets a shadow, glow or outline, and no shadow is a hard offset.

rules.name: The Square-Cut Paper Rule
rules.body: Sheets keep 2px corners and never round further; actions are always full pills. Nothing sits between those two shapes except inputs (4px) and the window itself (6px).

rules.name: The Tape Rule
rules.body: One strip of Gold Tape holds each sheet; the grade placard, the heaviest card, takes two. Each strip is 26px tall and cut to its own length (66–110px) and angle (between −33° and +11°), and overhangs a corner or the top edge by 6–15px. On phones the strips shrink to 20px tall and 52–70px long and flatten to within ±7°, so none reaches the lettering around the sheet.
